name: scifact
title: SciFact — scientific claim verification
why: The known-positives come from expert annotations rather than from this
repository. SciFact pairs a claim with the document whose sentences a
domain expert marked as supporting or contradicting it, which is exactly
the judgement pheasant's evaluation plane calls typed proof. A demo
corpus whose positives were written by the seeding script measures the
It is also the canonical small retrieval benchmark: SciFact is one of the
BEIR tasks, and is the dataset sentence-transformers, Vespa, Qdrant,
Weaviate, Haystack and LlamaIndex all report on.

source.paper: Wadden et al., 'Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims', EMNLP 2020

license.abstracts: from S2ORC; redistributed by the SciFact release
license.note: Fetched at benchmark time and never vendored into this repository.

why: A subset, and deliberately a *deterministic* one: the full 5,183
abstracts index in minutes, which is too slow for a screenshot run and
far past what a demo needs to make ranking matter.
The rule is stated so it cannot be cherry-picked to flatter a result:
take the first N dev claims that carry expert evidence, include every
document they cite, then fill the rest of the corpus with a seeded
sample of uncited abstracts. The decoys are what make rank matter —
a corpus where every query's answer is the only plausible document
